segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus left the temple and was going on his way when his disciples came up to point out to him the temple buildings.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the close of the age?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Watch out that no one leads you astray.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Messiah,’ and they will lead many astray.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are going to hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for this must happen, but it is not yet the end.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But all these are the beginning of the birth pains.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then they will hand you over to suffering and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of my name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then many will fall away, and they will hand one another over and hate one another.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And many false prophets will rise up and lead many astray.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And because lawlessness will increase, the love of most will grow cold.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the one who endures to the end will be saved.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of through the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: then those in Judea must flee to the mountains;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the one on the housetop must not go down to take what is in his house,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and the one in the field must not turn back to get his cloak.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on a Sabbath.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For then there will be great suffering, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, and never will be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if those days had not been cut short, no one would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones those days will be cut short.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Messiah!’ or ‘Here!’—do not believe it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For false messiahs and false prophets will rise up and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: See, I have told you beforehand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So if they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as the lightning comes out of the east and is seen as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Wherever the carcass is, there the vultures will gather.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Immediately after the suffering of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And he will send out his angels with a great trumpet blast, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: From the fig tree learn this parable: as soon as its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So you also, when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the very door.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But about that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son, but the Father alone.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For as the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, right up to the day Noah entered the ark,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and they knew nothing until the flood came and swept them all away, so too will the coming of the Son of Man be.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So stay awake, because you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But know this: if the master of the house had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have let his house be broken into.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason you also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Who then is the faithful and sensible slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household to give them their food at the proper time?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all that he owns.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if that bad slave says in his heart, ‘My master is a long time coming,’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and begins to beat his fellow slaves, and eats and drinks with the drunkards,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour that he does not know,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and will cut him in two and assign him his place with the hypocrites. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

notes.note: The Greek word means both arrival and presence, and was the regular term for the official visit of a king or emperor to a city. Matthew is the only Gospel to use it, four times in this chapter (verses 3, 27, 37, 39). 'Coming' is the standard rendering and is kept here.

The Greek word translates the Hebrew for 'anointed one', the king Israel expected. Here it is a title that pretenders claim for themselves, not a name, so 'Messiah' is used, as it is in verse 23 and in 'false messiahs' in verse 24. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels and keep 'Christ' where the word functions as a name.

The same Greek word, in the plural, is rendered 'Gentiles' elsewhere in this translation when it means the non-Jewish peoples. Here and in verses 9 and 14 the peoples of the world as political and ethnic units are in view, so 'nation' and 'nations' are used. Dividing the word by sense in this way is standard practice.

The word means pressure, and so distress or oppression of any kind; it was an ordinary word, not a technical term. The traditional 'tribulation' has become a label for a specific end-time period, which says more than the Greek does. The same word is used in verses 21 ('great suffering') and 29.

The word meant an announcement of good news, such as a victory or a ruler's accession, and the related verb is used in the Greek version of Isaiah for announcing God's reign. 'Gospel' is the traditional rendering and many translations keep it; others use 'good news', as here, because 'gospel' now sounds like a purely religious term.

The phrase comes from Daniel (9:27, 11:31, 12:11), where it describes something detestable that defiles the sanctuary and leaves it desolate. Jewish readers connected it with the pagan altar set up in the Jerusalem temple under Antiochus IV in 167 BC; 1 Maccabees 1:54 uses the same phrase for it. Jesus points to a further event of that kind. Which event is disputed, though many connect it with the Roman war of AD 66–70.

These words may be part of Jesus's speech, addressed to the reader of Daniel, or an aside by the evangelist to the person reading the Gospel aloud. The same words appear in Mark 13:14, where Daniel is not named, and many scholars take them as an editorial aside. The text here leaves them inside the speech.

The Greek is the ordinary word for someone or something chosen or picked out, and in the Septuagint it is used of Israel as God's chosen people. 'The elect' is the traditional rendering and means the same thing, but it now sounds like a technical theological term. Most major translations still use 'the elect'.

notes.traditional: it is near / he is near
notes.note: The Greek verb has no expressed subject, so the phrase could equally be 'it is near', meaning the end or the events just described. Translations are divided. 'He' is chosen here because the preceding verses describe the coming of the Son of Man, and the image of someone standing at the door suits a person.

Elsewhere in Matthew this phrase refers to Jesus's contemporaries, and that is its most natural sense here. Because the verse is hard to fit with a far-future reading of the chapter, some have proposed 'this race' or 'this kind of people', and others limit 'all these things' to the events leading up to the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70. The interpretation is disputed. The rendering itself is not seriously in doubt.

Many later manuscripts lack these words in Matthew, while important early witnesses include them. They are undisputed in the parallel at Mark 13:32. Most editors think copyists dropped them because of the difficulty of the Son not knowing, and the SBLGNT prints them.

The Greek word denotes a person owned by a master, not a hired employee, and a first-century hearer would have understood it that way. The traditional 'servant' softens this. Slaves could hold positions of considerable responsibility, as this household manager does. Many recent translations also use 'slave'.
